faq.a: Khalilah is associated with the Arabic form خليلة, whose core sense is friend, companion (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Khalilah?
faq.a: Khalilah is associated with Arabic. Khalilah is Arabic خَلِيلَة (Khalīla) 'friend, companion' (feminine), from the root خ ل ل (kh-l-l). The source gloss 'Friend of Allah' is broadly consistent.
Yes — the underlying form خليلة is Arabic.
Khalilah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Khalilah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Khalilah is rendered خلیلہ and carries the sense خلیلہ، دوست (مؤنث).

faq.q: What does Khalilah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Khalilah is rendered خلیله and carries the sense خلیله، دوست (مؤنث).
A romanized syllable approximation is kha-li-lah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Khalilah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Khalilah, khalilah. Script forms are خليلة, خلیله, خلیلہ, ख़लीला.

faq.q: Is Khalilah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
